The 7 Core Principles of Interior Design

To achieve a balanced and professional look, our specialists adhere to seven fundamental principles that guide every project. These principles ensure that even the most adventurous designs remain grounded in proven aesthetic theory, providing a sense of order and harmony within the home.

Achieving Perfect Balance and Symmetry

Balance is the distribution of visual weight in a room, which can be achieved through symmetrical, asymmetrical, or radial arrangements. In the East Atlanta area, we often use asymmetrical balance to create a more casual, modern feel that suits the neighborhood’s relaxed vibe.

  • Symmetrical Balance: Mirroring items on a central axis for a formal look.
  • Asymmetrical Balance: Using different objects with similar visual weight for a dynamic feel.
  • Radial Balance: Arranging items around a central focal point, like a round dining table.

Creating Focal Points and Emphasis

Every room needs a centerpiece that draws the eye and provides a starting point for the rest of the design. Whether it is a bold piece of local art or a fireplace, we help homeowners highlight these features to give the space a clear sense of purpose. A well-placed focal point can also help give your living room a fun refresh without requiring a total overhaul.

Establishing Rhythm and Visual Movement

Rhythm in design is about creating patterns of repetition and contrast to move the eye around the space. Our team uses color, texture, and line to create a sense of movement that keeps the room feeling energetic and cohesive. This prevents a space from feeling stagnant or cluttered, ensuring a smooth visual flow from one area to the next.

Essential Interior Design Rules: The 3-5-7 and 70-20-10 Methods

To create a balanced look, our team often utilizes mathematical rules that help guide color selection and accessory placement. These methods ensure that your home close to East Atlanta looks professionally styled rather than cluttered. Whether you are choosing furniture upholstery or new wallpaper, these rules provide a solid foundation.

  1. Apply the 70-20-10 rule for color: 70% dominant color, 20% secondary color, and 10% accent color.
  2. Use the “Rule of Three” when styling shelves or coffee tables to create visual interest.
  3. Group objects in odd numbers (3, 5, or 7) to make arrangements feel more natural and less forced.
  4. Ensure the accent color (the 10%) is distributed evenly throughout the room to pull the design together.
